summary: Extends the Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol, which tunnels PPP sessions, so it can carry information about why a call or session was disconnected.

eli5.summary: It adds a note to a hung-up phone call explaining why it ended.

what is the difference between lac and lns
subtitle: A new L2TP attribute that tells a peer why a PPP session ended, for logging and debugging.

tldr.problem: L2TP hides PPP details and its Result and Error Codes only describe L2TP-specific problems, so a host cannot tell its peer why the PPP session was disconnected.
tldr.mechanism: A new AVP, the PPP Disconnect Cause Code (type 46), goes in the Call-Disconnect-Notify message and carries a disconnect code, a PPP control protocol number, a direction and optional human-readable text.
tldr.outcome: Operators get descriptive information for accounting and debugging, especially when the two L2TP hosts are run by different parties. The AVP is informational and does not change tunnel or session behavior.

today: RFC 3145 is a Proposed Standard, published in July 2001. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Disconnect Causes Are Needed
sections.content:
L2TP tunnels PPP over various media and, by design, shields itself from the details of the PPP session. Sometimes a L2TP host (an L2TP Access Concentrator, LAC, or L2TP Network Server, LNS) benefits from PPP-specific disconnect information in a descriptive form. The lack of it is especially a problem when the LAC and LNS are not owned or managed by the same entities.

The existing L2TP Result and Error Codes only cover L2TP-specific reasons. This RFC adds the PPP Disconnect Cause Code AVP, which MAY be used alongside them and not in place of them. It must not affect the tunnel or the PPP session, and exists for informational and logging purposes.
sections.eli5: The tunnel already says when its own part broke. This adds a way to say why the inside conversation ended too.

sections.title: The PPP Disconnect Cause Code AVP
sections.content:
The AVP is valid only in the Call-Disconnect-Notify (CDN) message and MUST NOT be marked Mandatory. It uses Vendor ID 0 and Attribute Type 46. The Value must be at least 11 octets long. Any extra octets hold descriptive text in UTF-8 that can be shown to a user or written to a log.

After the standard AVP header come a two-octet Disconnect Code, a two-octet Control Protocol Number (the PPP control protocol primarily involved, if any) and a one-octet Direction. Direction is 0 for a global error, 1 for at peer and 2 for at local; 3 to 255 are reserved. Direction SHOULD be 0 unless a specific code documents otherwise. The Hidden bit MAY be set.
sections.eli5: The note has a reason number, a label for which part of the conversation failed, a side (me or you) and optional plain words.

sections.title: The Disconnect Codes
sections.content:
The codes fall into four groups. Global errors (0 to 4) are not tied to one control protocol, so the Control Protocol Number MUST be 0. They include no information (0), administrative disconnect (1), a missing proxy LCP at the LNS (2), a normal disconnect after an LCP Terminate-Request (3) and refused compulsory encryption (4).

LCP errors (5 to 12) cover link negotiation failures such as FSM timeout, no recognizable LCP packets, a Magic Number error with a possibly looped-back link, an Echo Request timeout, unexpected Multilink PPP bundle parameters and refused compulsory call-back. The Control Protocol Number MUST be C021 hexadecimal.

Authentication errors (13 to 16) include unacceptable authentication protocols and failed authentication, using the number of the authentication protocol in use. NCP errors (17 to 20) cover network protocol negotiation, such as no NCPs reaching Opened state or failure to converge on addresses. Several copies of the AVP MAY be sent when multiple network protocols fail.
sections.eli5: The reasons are sorted into four boxes: general, link trouble, password trouble and network-setup trouble.

sections.title: Who Sends It and Older Drafts
sections.content:
Either the LNS or the LAC may send this AVP. It is expected to be most useful as a notification from the LNS to the LAC in the compulsory tunneling case, though other uses are not precluded.

A draft form of the AVP used Vendor ID 43 (3Com Corporation) with vendor-specific Attribute Type 46. Implementations MAY accept these as equivalent but SHOULD NOT transmit them.
sections.eli5: Either end can send the note, and the server telling the access box is the most common case. Older drafts used a different label, which should only be read, never sent.

sections.title: Security and IANA Registry
sections.content:
The AVP relies on the underlying L2TP security mechanisms for integrity and confidentiality, and it MAY be hidden as described in section 4.3 of RFC 2661. The RFC says the extension gives an attacker no useful information, and warns that future codes should not reveal, for example, that an authentication name is correct while the password is wrong.

IANA assigned Attribute Type 46. Disconnect Codes 0 to 20 are defined here. Codes 21 to 32767 are assigned subject to IESG Approval, 32768 to 65279 on a First Come First Served basis for vendor-specific features, and 65280 to 65535 are for Private or Experimental Use.
sections.eli5: The note is only for logs and shows nothing a snoop could use, but it can be hidden. Number ranges are set aside for official, vendor and experimental reasons.
